result.summary: The residential street provides continuous sidewalks and a marked midblock crosswalk, offering basic pedestrian access. However, the wide roadway and extensive on-street parking create potential visibility hazards and may encourage higher vehicle speeds.

hazards.name: Parked vehicles near crosswalk
hazards.description: Parked cars on both sides of the street obstruct the view between pedestrians and drivers at the crosswalk.

hazards.name: Wide, unmarked roadway
hazards.description: The lack of lane markings and the overall width of the street can encourage higher vehicle speeds in a residential zone.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Install curb extensions to shorten the crossing distance and improve visibility by preventing parking too close to the crosswalk.

interventions.title: Speed Humps
interventions.description: Implement speed humps to reduce vehicle speeds and improve safety for pedestrians crossing the street.

interventions.title: Daylighting
interventions.description: Remove parking spaces immediately adjacent to the crosswalk to ensure clear sight lines for all road users.

result.summary: This residential environment features narrow streets and row housing with a basic sidewalk on at least one side. While traffic speeds are likely low due to the narrow roadway and a posted speed hump sign, pedestrians face obstructions from utility poles and parked vehicles that limit walkway width and visibility.

hazards.name: Sidewalk Obstruction
hazards.description: A utility pole is located directly in the path of the sidewalk, significantly narrowing the effective walking width.
hazards.location_in_image: Left foreground, on the sidewalk next to the brick building.

hazards.name: Sightline Obstruction
hazards.description: The parked SUV obscures the view between pedestrians on the sidewalk and vehicles exiting the narrow alleyway.
hazards.location_in_image: Foreground, parked along the curb blocking the view of the alley entrance.

interventions.title: Daylighting
interventions.description: Remove the parking space immediately adjacent to the alley entrance to improve sightlines between drivers and pedestrians.

interventions.title: Sidewalk Widening or Obstacle Relocation
interventions.description: Relocate the utility pole or widen the sidewalk to ensure a continuous, unobstructed clear path for pedestrians, including those with mobility aids.

interventions.title: Marked Crosswalk
interventions.description: Install a marked crosswalk across the alley entrance to clearly define pedestrian priority and alert drivers to the crossing point.

result.summary: This residential street features a narrow, poorly maintained sidewalk on the left and lacks a clear, dedicated pedestrian walkway on the right. The wide, straight roadway with on-street parking on both sides lacks traffic calming or marked crossings, creating a car-centric environment with limited pedestrian protection.

hazards.name: Narrow and Obstructed Sidewalk
hazards.description: The sidewalk on the left is very narrow and partially obstructed by overgrown vegetation and fencing, forcing pedestrians into a confined space.

hazards.name: Missing Sidewalk
hazards.description: The right side of the street lacks a clearly defined, continuous sidewalk, potentially forcing pedestrians to walk in the roadway or on private property.

hazards.name: Visual Obstructions from Parked Cars
hazards.description: Parallel parked cars on both sides of the street can block sightlines between drivers and pedestrians attempting to cross.

interventions.title: Sidewalk Expansion and Repair
interventions.description: Install a continuous, ADA-compliant sidewalk on both sides of the street with a minimum width of 5 feet.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Install curb extensions at intersections to shorten crossing distances and improve visibility between pedestrians and drivers.

interventions.title: Traffic Calming Measures
interventions.description: Implement speed humps or cushions to reduce vehicle speeds on this straight residential stretch.

result.summary: The pedestrian environment is a typical residential street with row housing and minimal safety infrastructure. While sidewalks are present, they are narrow and lack buffers, and the wide, unmarked roadway lacks designated crossing points or traffic calming measures.

hazards.name: Visual Obstruction from Parked Cars
hazards.description: Parked vehicles on the right side of the alley entrance block sightlines between pedestrians exiting the alley and drivers on the main road.
hazards.location_in_image: Right side of the alley entrance where the blue SUV and silver truck are parked.

hazards.name: Lack of Marked Crossing
hazards.description: There are no marked crosswalks or signage to facilitate safe pedestrian crossing across the wide roadway.

hazards.name: Wide Unmarked Roadway
hazards.description: The lack of lane markings on a relatively wide street can encourage higher vehicle speeds and unpredictable lane positioning.

interventions.title: Daylighting at Alley Entrance
interventions.description: Remove parking spaces immediately adjacent to the alley entrance to improve visibility for all road users.

interventions.title: Marked Crosswalk and Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Install a high-visibility marked crosswalk with curb extensions to reduce crossing distance and improve pedestrian visibility.

interventions.description: Implement speed humps or speed cushions to reduce vehicle speeds in this residential area.
